name: open the pull request and post the plan on it
about: Push the branch and open the PR. THE DESCRIPTION IS A DURABLE ARTIFACT AND NOT A SENTENCE, and it is a DIFFERENT artifact from the plan comment below: the comment is written for the human about to review this change, the description for whoever reads the repository a year from now with none of the context you have. It carries, each in a line or two: WHY the change exists; the ROOT CAUSE where there was a defect, or the FEATURE INTENT and what the new behaviour is specified to do where there was not; the SELECTED SOLUTION and the tradeoffs that actually mattered; the BEHAVIOUR CHANGES a user or another system will see; the SCOPE, with the exclusions that change what anybody should expect; the VERIFICATION and the INDEPENDENT REVIEW completed, each named by the commit it covered; and the RISKS accepted or deferred. DRAW IT FROM THE RECORD, DO NOT RE-AUTHOR IT — `cause`, `solution`, `scope`, `limitations`, `verification` and `review` are already on the change record, and a description that says something subtly different from the record is a second account of one change that somebody downstream has to reconcile. Where a field is filled, the description is a shorter reading of it and nothing else. CONCISE, AND IT LINKS RATHER THAN REPRODUCES: the plan, the review findings and the raw evidence are one comment and one record away, so a description that pastes them is one nobody finishes reading. None of these is a heading you must type — a small change is a short description with the parts that are empty left out, and seven empty sections read worse than four true sentences. Then comment the plan onto it, with this step's `command` as it stands — that ONE plan and never the store, posted as the markdown it gives you, no fenced block, no summarising, no reformatting. It renders the plan AS IT STANDS AT THAT MOMENT — open steps, empty `output` fields and all — and waits for nothing: no step has to be finished first, and `merge` does this same marked upsert again as it lands, editing the comment in place. So a definition telling you that some field of its own is what this comment dumps is saying why that field must be filled, never that the comment waits for it. The command is on the step so nobody has to reconstruct it; fill in the PR number and the plan id and run it. Obliges `change-approval`, which obliges `review`, AND `merge-human-review`, so naming this step lands FOUR steps in one act — and each lands where it runs rather than where it was named: change approval is an early root before implementation; implementation review and the human-only checklist follow the completed work; this step waits on all three. That is what makes the first PR comment ready for its human reader rather than opening before their checklist exists. Nothing about those deps needs fixing afterwards, provided the implementation is already in the plan when you name this: a step is placed against the plan as it stands, and nothing already in it is re-deped. WHAT IT REQUIRES, read from the change record rather than rerun: a CURRENT verification (`verification`, naming the commit it covers), a RESOLVED review (`review`, no unresolved major), and the human-only checks or the explicit answer that none remain — the evidence is already there, so this reads it by identity and does not run it again. A DIRECT change reaches its PR here too, without any of the steps above: it has no plan, so there is no `change-approval` to oblige and no library step to name — its record is posted with this same `sb plugin plans comment <record> --pr <PR>`, and the record is what carries the human request, the verification and the review onto the pull request. REFRESHED, NOT ONLY AT MERGE. The comment is this command run again whenever what a human should see materially changes — a reviewer's fix, the reviewed head moving, a landing decision — so its first screenful stays true to the current state rather than the state at the open. `merge` does the last one itself, after it has recorded how the landing went; the updates between are posted as they land.
